header:
Date: 2027-09-27
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood, AE); Priya Anand (Redwood, SE); Evelyn Shaw (Obelisk, Head of Infra); Marcus Li (Obelisk, Security Eng); Diane Powers (Obelisk, PM)
Recording: cloud.recordings/ff/ff-20270927-obl-01.mp3
summary: Initial security posture intake focused on SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML integration with Okta, RBAC and least-privilege model, audit log retention/forwarding, and encryption/KMS options for hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments. Customer leaning toward dedicated or VPC private deployment for sensitive PII workloads; wants pilot and bench to prove latency and auditability. Next steps: SOC2 docs, benchmark, SAML metadata, pilot criteria.
topics: SOC2/ISO evidence; SSO (Okta, SAML, SCIM); RBAC role mapping; audit logs (retention, export, immutability); encryption at rest/in transit; KMS options (BYOK, customer-managed KMS, HSM); hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs; data residency and retention policies; pilot/benchmark plan
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining — i'm jordan meyers with Redwood, i'm the AE on this account, and with me is priya our solutions engineer. um we'll start with a quick intake — what you're protecting and what gating criteria you have for hosting.
[00:22] Evelyn: hi, thanks. i'm evelyn, head of infra at Obelisk. we run retail payments and customer profiles, there's definitely pii involved. primary ask is auditability and encryption controls, plus single sign-on. we've got a SOC 2 Type II program and we're ISO-curious.
[00:35] Marcus: yeah, hi, marcus here. main concerns: where logs live, who can access model payloads, key management, and retention policies. also gotta know if we can keep keys in our AWS KMS/HSM.
[00:47] Priya: absolutely. quick note on terminology — when we say Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private: Hosted is Redwood-managed multi-tenant API, Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with isolation, and Private is VPC or on-prem with a private control plane. you can integrate customer KMS in Dedicated via VPC peering or choose Private for fully customer-managed keys.
[01:06] Marcus: when you say "integrate", what does that mean practically? is it BYOK or do you hold the keys and you wrap them?
[01:13] Priya: good question. we support BYOK for Private deployments — the control plane can be configured to talk to your KMS over a secure endpoint, and you get envelope encryption. for Dedicated (hosted but isolated), we offer an option to use customer-managed keys in your cloud account via cross-account grants — it's not available for multi-tenant Hosted at the moment. HSM-backed keys are supported in the Private package.
[01:34] Marcus: okay. also, how granular is RBAC? we want least-privilege — engineers shouldn't be able to pull raw transcripts unless they have a compliance role.
[01:42] Jordan: we have role-based access with pre-built roles and custom roles. Priya, want to take the RBAC details?
[01:46] Priya: yeah. so out of the box we have roles: admin, operator, auditor, developer. admin can do everything, operator can deploy models and manage capacity, auditor is read-only on logs and transcripts, developer can call APIs but not access audit trails. you can map SAML groups from Okta to these roles, and there's SCIM for provisioning.
[02:05] Diane: so we can map our existing Okta groups to Redwood roles — good. what about session recordings and audit logs, retention windows?
[02:13] Priya: logs are configurable. default for Hosted is 90 days for audit logs and 30 for transient request traces, but for Dedicated/Private you can set retention to 365 days or push logs to your S3/Syslog or SIEM. We also support write-once export snapshots for compliance checks.
[02:31] Marcus: are audit logs tamper-evident? we need to prove immutability for some audits.
[02:36] Priya: yes — for Private we can write logs to an append-only S3 bucket with object lock, and we support log signing. For Dedicated we provide signed exports and can stream to your SIEM; the hosted multi-tenant model has signed retention windows but you'd likely pick Dedicated or Private for immutability needs.
[02:55] Evelyn: we have EU residency requirements for a subset of data. can you pin region and ensure data never leaves eu-west-1?
[03:02] Jordan: yes — region pinning is supported. Private deployments can be stood up in your VPC in the EU region, and Dedicated capacity can be assigned to region-specific pools. hosted global API is routed by policy so you need to use a region-specific endpoint for strict residency.
[03:17] Marcus: encryption in transit — do you enforce TLS 1.2+? any mTLS for control plane?
[03:22] Priya: TLS 1.2+ enforced, we recommend TLS 1.3; control plane to data plane uses mTLS in Dedicated/Private by default.
[03:30] Marcus: ok good. another thing: tokenization and PII redaction — do you provide PII-aware redaction before logs are stored?
[03:36] Priya: we have configurable redaction pipelines. you can mask or redact specific classes of data before it's written to logs. that pipeline can run inline in the Private deployment or as a post-processing job in Dedicated. Hosted has a standard PII scrub but for strict needs you'd use Dedicated with a custom scrubber.
[03:53] Jordan: do you have any regulatory auditors or evidence, evelyn, that we should include up front?
[03:57] Evelyn: we already collect SOC 2 Type II, we run quarterly internal audits, and we are starting an ISO 27001 gap assessment. we need to see your SOC 2 artifacts and an explanation of any exceptions.
[04:10] Jordan: for sure — i'll send the SOC 2 Type II pack and an ISO 27001 summary later today. it includes our control matrix, pen test summary, and subservice orgs.
[04:18] Marcus: regarding SAML, we use Okta and have multiple groups. can we get SCIM to auto-provision?
[04:24] Priya: yes, SCIM provisioning works with our SAML integration. we map Okta groups to roles and can auto-provision accounts. we also support Just-In-Time (JIT) provisioning if you don't want SCIM.
[04:34] Diane: are login events and admin actions included in audit logs? do you log token issuance and service account actions?
[04:41] Priya: yes, login events, token issuance, API key creation, role changes, model rollouts — all are captured. timestamps, IP, user agent, and change diffs are stored for each event.
[04:51] Marcus: what about lighting up a separate read-only log for auditors? we want to avoid giving auditors live admin access.
[04:57] Priya: totally — you can create an auditor export bucket or give the auditor IAM read-only access to logs. we also produce periodic signed snapshots that you can hand off to auditors without granting runtime access.
[05:07] [pause, multiple voices]
[05:12] Evelyn: cost question — if we do Dedicated with customer KMS and extra logging, how much premium vs hosted?
[05:18] Jordan: ballpark: Dedicated pricing is a capacity/commit model — there's a baseline reserve plus premium for BYOK and longer retention. depends on GPU shape and qps; priya will model this in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[05:28] Priya: i'll put together a per-token / per-hour cost delta with options: hosted baseline, dedicated with BYOK, private on customer infra. we'll include the cost of log egress and S3 retention in that spreadsheet.
[05:36] Marcus: does Redwood keep transcripts for prompt/response for model quality monitoring? we want to know retention and who can view them.
[05:42] Priya: yes, transcript storage is part of the platform used for evals and regresses. retention is configurable; you can opt-out of storing transcripts in Hosted, or in Dedicated/Private you can set it to zero retention and forward raw inputs to your S3 if you want. Access is governed by RBAC so only auditor roles see them. note: redaction can be applied prior to storage.
[06:02] Diane: for the pilot we'll need an SLA target and a rollback plan if latency is bad. what's typical p95 on dedicated?
[06:09] Priya: with a tuned model and KV caching enabled, we've seen p95 < 120ms for 8k context popular models on RTX A100-equivalent pools. but depends heavily on prompt patterns and cache hit rate. we'll run the 500 qps profile against your sample prompts to give you realistic numbers.
[06:26] Marcus: about KV cache — is that per-tenant and how is it persisted?
[06:31] Priya: KV cache is per-deployment/tenant and sits on NVMe-backed local shards. for Dedicated you get warm cache within your pool; on Private you control persistence policy. it's encrypted at rest. sometimes the transcript shows it as "kay vee cache" in the notes, so don't worry if the automated transcript mangles it.
[06:47] Jordan: quick check — any blockers to sharing Okta metadata and doing the pilot?
[06:51] Marcus: none on our side. i'll need to run the legal checklist but i'll share the SAML metadata.
[06:56] Diane: timeline wise, procurement needs a week after the pilot to evaluate. so we want pilot early october.
[07:02] Jordan: that aligns — we'll aim to have the bench results and SOC pack before then.
[07:06] [10-minute deep dive later in call into audit schema and SIEM integration]
[17:18] Priya: when streaming logs to your SIEM we expose a structured schema: event_type, actor_id, action, resource, before/after, timestamp, request_id, latency_ms. you can map those fields into Splunk/Datadog. we also provide a JSON schema and example payloads in the security docs.
[17:36] Marcus: can we get an example with PII fields masked? we need to show auditors.
[17:40] Priya: yes — i'll attach examples. note the scrubber can either redact client-side in Private, or in Dedicated we can run it in a dedicated scrubber stage before archival.
[17:51] Marcus: how about secure deletion? sometimes legal asks for permanent deletion of certain records after X days.
[17:56] Priya: we support retention lifecycles and secure deletion workflows; for Private you can run deletion scripts in-place; for Dedicated we can schedule secure deletion and purge from backups with certs. hosted multi-tenant has stricter constraints so for compliance deletion windows we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[18:12] Evelyn: i want to confirm the audit trail for administrative actions — is there a separate encryption key or is it the same KMS?
[18:18] Priya: typically audit logs are encrypted with a distinct key material and you can opt to have that in your KMS. we'll document recommended key separation in the SOC pack.
[18:27] Jordan: any other gating controls?
[18:29] Marcus: data residency for EU items and SSO integration are the main two. also want proof that the app can't call out to third-party telemetry without our consent.
[18:36] Priya: we can turn off outbound telemetry and opt into explicit telemetry buckets. we document every outbound domain in the security pack.
[18:42] Diane: who signs the BAA / DPA? procurement will want a legal contact.
[18:47] Jordan: i'll loop in our legal team; i'll send a draft DPA and sample BAA.
[18:51] [cross-talk, short break in call]
[19:10] Marcus: tiny nit — for SIEM streaming, do you support batching to reduce cost or is it real-time only?
[19:15] Priya: both — we support near real-time streaming and batched exports to S3 for cost optimization. you can choose which events stream and which ones batch.
[19:23] Marcus: nice. also, does Redwood provide a way to prove that model weights are not exfiltrated? we need to understand boundaries between customer data and model artifact updates.
[19:33] Priya: models are versioned and model updates are handled by our runtime. customer data never enters model training pipelines — we provide written attestations in the SOC2 artifacts. for absolute isolation you'd pick Private where training/ops access can be restricted.
[19:50] Evelyn: will you provide proof-of-concept with some synthetic data to verify no leakage?
[19:55] Priya: yes, the pilot can include a synthetic leak test and we can run a small red-team evaluation as part of the benchmark.
[20:02] Diane: ok good. next up — retention policy examples? give us a few presets?
[20:07] Jordan: common presets: Hosted default (audit 90d, traces 30d), Dedicated standard (audit 365d, traces 90d), Private custom (any). we can produce a retention matrix.
[20:18] Marcus: will you include egress cost estimates? that's part of procurement's model.
[20:23] Priya: yes, egress for logs to S3/SIEM and cross-region replication will be included in the cost model.
[20:29] [longer technical digression on KMS grants and cross-account permissions]
[29:40] Priya: practically, for cross-account KMS we provide a managed IAM role you grant to Redwood with a limited set of decrypt/encrypt permissions; that role is used by our runtime to unwrap keys for ephemeral use. for Private you keep keys entirely behind your network.
[29:59] Marcus: are KMS requests logged separately? we need key usage logs.
[30:04] Priya: yes — KMS access events go to CloudTrail (or equivalent) and we can correlate them with our request IDs for audits.
[30:12] Marcus: perfect.
[30:15] Jordan: small admin question — who on your side will be the day-to-day?
[30:18] Diane: product will coordinate pilots, evelyn will own infra, and marcus will own security gating.
[30:24] Jordan: cool — i'll tag them in the action items.
[30:28] [closing 10 minutes: recap & next steps]
[39:10] Jordan: recap — i'll send SOC2, ISO summary, DPA draft; priya will run the 500 qps bench and produce cost/latency spreadsheet; marcus will share Okta metadata and RBAC matrix; diane will confirm pilot acceptance criteria.
[39:25] Marcus: timeline: we'll aim to collect procurement feedback after pilot and procurement will want an itemized cost delta to present to finance.
[39:33] Jordan: great. any last questions?
[39:36] Evelyn: can you also surface sample SIEM mapping files? that's helpful.
[39:40] Priya: yes, i'll include Splunk/Datadog mapping and an example SIEM ingestion config.
[39:46] Diane: thanks everyone.
[39:48] Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up by email with docs and schedule.
[39:52] [end recording — meeting closed]
